chapter: South America and back in New York
title: Business contact with whites, never at home
summary: Wooding says he met whites like Lyons only in restaurants and clubs, never homes, and refused invitations that expected him to perform.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: I just wanted to ask you. People like Mr. Lyons, people like that. The white people who were on the business end of it. Your contact, when I say your contact, I don't mean just you, but other musicians and bandleaders -- was it strictly a business contact? Would you ever be invited to Lyons' home, for instance, for dinner? Or would you ever socialize with the white people?
Why do you say I stayed in Europe so long? Because today, you can meet him at the Park Sheraton or same hotel, something like that, but you'll never get to his home.

You can count those that would come to his home -- in fact, I don't know of any. So really, it's a bad business association. Because, like, I'm sitting in your home, now. But how many homes could I sit in. Because a lot of transactions -- I told you when I went to Europe. That deal was pulled off in a club or a restaurant at four o'clock in the morning. Well, now picture me in Arthur Lyons home. I don't even know where he lives. We always met outside. Of course,
that line is much better than it has been, but we've all had a -- it's oil and water. East is East and West is West, and never the twain shall meet.
Right. Now, I've heard this from many musicians. That the only time they were invited to anyone's home was when they were expected to perform.
Yeah. And that's what I hated. If I thought I was invited somewhere so that I could give my musical services, my artistic end of it, I never would go.

See, because I didn't like that. And I was very happy -- that's one reason I was very happy to go back to Europe. And I would have no doubt made it my home, but I had relatives back here in the States, and I wanted to see them, and they didn't have enough money to come to see me. So that's what brought me back.
